/-!
# Conjecture 8.78

by B. Hartley

It is known that there exists a countable locally finite group that contains a copy of
every other countable locally finite group (P. Hall's universal locally finite group).
For which other classes of countable groups does a similar "largest" group exist?
In particular, what about periodic locally soluble groups? periodic locally nilpotent
groups?

We formalise the two special cases singled out in the statement. A group is *periodic*
if every element has finite order, *locally soluble* if every finitely generated subgroup
is soluble, and *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent.
A group $G$ *contains a copy* of a group $H$ if $H$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $G$,
that is, if there is an injective group homomorphism $H \to G$. "Countable" is `Countable`,
so finite groups are included; this gives a statement equivalent to the countably infinite
reading, since a universal group is necessarily infinite and every finite group in either
class embeds in a countably infinite group of the same class.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

claims.decomposer_note: Open-ended request to describe the classes of countable groups admitting a universal member (a countable group in the class into which every countable group of the class embeds, as Hall's universal locally finite group does for locally finite groups); the deliverable is the description itself and no candidate answer is asserted, so there is no Prop to state.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question: does there exist a countable periodic (torsion) locally soluble group G such that every countable periodic locally soluble group is isomorphic to a subgroup of G? 'Countable' from 'classes of countable groups' applies both to G and to the embedded groups, 'copy' means an injective group homomorphism/isomorphic subgroup, and 'locally soluble' (every finitely generated subgroup is soluble) is not in Mathlib and needs a definition.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates encode the same mathematics: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ countable torsion (Monoid.IsTorsion) locally soluble group G : Type such that every countable torsion locally soluble group H admits an injective hom H →* G, with 'locally soluble' defined as every Subgroup.FG subgroup being IsSolvable. Quantifier order (∃ G ∀ H ∃ f), use of ∧ after the existential (not trivially true), positive-answer direction, and non-vacuous ∀ H all check out. c04 chosen as base because it follows the sibling Kourovka naming convention (kourovka.«8.78».parts.i in namespace Kourovka.«8.78»), has clear docstrings, and includes three proved @[category API] lemmas testing the bespoke definitions as CONTRIBUTING.md requests. I added one docstring sentence explaining the `Countable` (includes finite) reading and why it is equivalent to the countably infinite reading.
claims.source_text: In particular, what about periodic locally soluble groups?
claims.text_span: In particular, what about periodic locally soluble groups?

claims.decomposer_note: Same yes/no question for the class of countable periodic locally nilpotent groups (every finitely generated subgroup nilpotent, which also needs a definition); co-equal with part i as the second special case the statement singles out, while the general classification question is dropped.
claims.reviewer_why: Same shape as part i with IsLocallyNilpotent (every Subgroup.FG subgroup satisfies Group.IsNilpotent). Identical across all candidates modulo binder style and naming; c04 chosen for the same reasons as part i.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The two singled-out special cases are the only statable Props; the general 'for which other classes' question is rightly dropped. The opening sentence about locally finite groups is background (Hall's theorem), not a question, and is only mentioned in the module docstring.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.78

by B. Hartley

It is known that there exists a countable locally finite group that contains a copy of
every other countable locally finite group (P. Hall's universal locally finite group).
For which other classes of countable groups does a similar "largest" group exist?
In particular, what about periodic locally soluble groups? periodic locally nilpotent
groups?

We formalise the two special cases singled out in the statement. A group is *periodic*
if every element has finite order, *locally soluble* if every finitely generated subgroup
is soluble, and *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent.
A group $G$ *contains a copy* of a group $H$ if $H$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $G$,
that is, if there is an injective group homomorphism $H \to G$. "Countable" is `Countable`,
so finite groups are included; this gives a statement equivalent to the countably infinite
reading, since a universal group is necessarily infinite and every finite group in either
class embeds in a countably infinite group of the same class.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.78»

/-- A group is *locally soluble* if every finitely generated subgroup is soluble. -/
def IsLocallySolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsSolvable H

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A soluble group is locally soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallySolvable.of_isSolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsSolvable G] :
    IsLocallySolvable G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.IsNilpotent G] :
    IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A locally nilpotent group is locally soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.isLocallySolvable {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsLocallyNilpotent G) :
    IsLocallySolvable G :=
  fun H hH => have := h H hH; inferInstance

/--
Does there exist a countable periodic locally soluble group $G$ that contains a copy of
every countable periodic locally soluble group, i.e. such that for every countable periodic
locally soluble group $H$ there is an injective group homomorphism $H \to G$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.78».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Countable G ∧ Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧ IsLocallySolvable G ∧
      ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], Countable H → Monoid.IsTorsion H → IsLocallySolvable H →
        ∃ f : H →* G, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

/--
Does there exist a countable periodic locally nilpotent group $G$ that contains a copy of
every countable periodic locally nilpotent group, i.e. such that for every countable periodic
locally nilpotent group $H$ there is an injective group homomorphism $H \to G$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.78».parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Countable G ∧ Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧ IsLocallyNilpotent G ∧
      ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], Countable H → Monoid.IsTorsion H → IsLocallyNilpotent H →
        ∃ f : H →* G, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.78»

items: 'Periodic' is rendered as Monoid.IsTorsion (every element has finite order), the standard meaning in the Kourovka Notebook.
'Contains a copy of' is rendered as the existence of an injective group homomorphism H →* G (equivalently, H is isomorphic to a subgroup of G).

'Countable' is Lean's Countable, which includes finite groups; this matches the group-theoretic usage (e.g. Hall's universal locally finite group contains every finite group). Both the universal group G and the embedded groups H are required to be countable, following the decomposition notes and 'classes of countable groups'.
Both G and H are quantified over Type (universe 0). Since every countable group is isomorphic to one in Type, this loses no generality.
'Locally X' is defined as 'every finitely generated subgroup is X'. For the subgroup-closed classes soluble/nilpotent this agrees with the alternative 'every finite subset lies in an X-subgroup'.
Quantifier structure is ∃ G, (props of G) ∧ ∀ H, (props of H) → ∃ f, using ∧ (not →) after the existential, so the statement is not trivially true; answer(True) means a largest group exists.

Three short `@[category API]` lemmas (soluble ⇒ locally soluble, nilpotent ⇒ locally nilpotent, locally nilpotent ⇒ locally soluble) are included as basic API tests of the new definitions, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks; they are proved, not sorried.

The bespoke definitions live in the problem file (inside namespace Kourovka.«8.78») because the task restricts output to a single file; a reviewer may prefer moving them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

reviewer_notes: No candidate omitted any slot; all compiled. Differences were cosmetic only: `(_ : Countable G)`/`[Countable H]` binders vs `Countable G ∧`/`Countable H →` (equivalent), `Group.FG H` vs `H.FG` (equivalent by Group.fg_iff_subgroup_fg), theorem naming (`parts.i` vs `kourovka.«8.78».parts.i`), and presence of API lemmas. Modeling choices in the final file: 'periodic' = Monoid.IsTorsion; 'countable' = Countable (includes finite groups — equivalent to the countably-infinite reading since a universal G must be infinite and any finite H in either class embeds in H × Prüfer group, which remains in the class); 'copy' = injective group hom; 'locally X' = every finitely generated subgroup is X (equivalent to 'every finite subset lies in an X-subgroup' since soluble/nilpotent are subgroup-closed); groups in `Type` (no loss for countable groups). Bespoke definitions IsLocallySolvable / IsLocallyNilpotent kept in the problem file (as sibling 1_40.lean does); a maintainer might prefer moving them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. The general 'for which other classes' question was dropped per the decomposition table. Status 'open' taken as given by the task; the notebook statement provided carries no solution remark.
